newsitem.title: JAPAN: Special JGBs to cut JNR debt not feasible -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Special JGBs to cut JNR debt not feasible -- MOF.

text.p: Issuing special Japanese government bonds (JGBs) to reduce the debt of the former Japanese National Railways (JNR) is not feasible, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Tuesday.
A subcommittee of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party discussed measures to reduce the JNR debt in April, including a plan to issue inheritance-tax-free JGBs with no coupon.
"A sale by the government of such financial instruments would be unfair as it would benefit only a limited number of taxpayers," the MOF official said.
"Those special JGBs would be targeted at wealthy individual taxpayers," he said.
The debt of JNR Settlement Corp, a state-owned agent in charge of selling the assets of the former JNR, totalled 28.1 trillion yen as of April 1, up from 27.6 trillion a year earlier.
The LDP subcommittee has discussed other measures to cut JNR Settlement Corp's debt, such as a reduction in interest payments to the government's fiscal investment and loan programme.
A spokesman for the LDP said on Tuesday that the subcommittee would finalise a draft plan by early June.
